organizations.name: Government of Bangladesh
organizations.description: Central government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh. Since February 2026 led by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party following the 12 February 2026 general election, which ended the caretaker administration of Chief Adviser Muhammad Yunus.

organizations.name: Tarique Rahman ministry
organizations.description: 25th cabinet of Bangladesh (the collective executive body, also known as the Cabinet of Bangladesh), formed 17 February 2026 after the BNP won the 2026 general election. Coalition of BNP with minor allies; Jamaat-e-Islami is the parliamentary opposition. Expanded to 52 members in August 2026.

key_people.title: Prime Minister (also Defence; PMO; Cabinet Division)
key_people.name: Tarique Rahman

key_people.title: Minister of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs
key_people.name: Md. Asaduzzaman

organizations.name: Prime Minister's Office (Bangladesh)
organizations.description: Government office supporting the Prime Minister of Bangladesh in coordinating the work of the Cabinet and ministries.

organizations.name: Jatiya Sangsad
organizations.description: National parliament of Bangladesh. The 13th Jatiya Sangsad was elected on 12 February 2026; BNP holds a two-thirds majority and Hafiz Uddin Ahmad was elected Speaker in March 2026. Constitution provides for 350 members (300 elected + 50 reserved seats).

organizations.name: Senate of Bangladesh
organizations.description: Proposed upper house of the Bangladesh Parliament, provided for under the post-2024 constitutional reform package (July Charter reforms incl. bicameralism put to the February 2026 referendum). Still listed as proposed, not yet operational.

organizations.name: Supreme Court of Bangladesh
organizations.description: Highest court of Bangladesh, comprising the Appellate Division and the High Court Division; heads the judiciary of Bangladesh.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Election Commission
organizations.description: Independent constitutional body responsible for conducting national and local elections in Bangladesh; administered the February 2026 general election.

organizations.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Bangladesh)
organizations.description: Government ministry of Bangladesh responsible for foreign policy and diplomatic missions. Headed since February 2026 by technocrat minister Khalilur Rahman.

organizations.name: Ministry of Finance (Bangladesh)
organizations.description: Government ministry of Bangladesh responsible for fiscal policy, the national budget and the treasury; Finance and Planning portfolios held by Amir Khasru Mahmud Chowdhury since February 2026.

organizations.name: Ministry of Home Affairs (Bangladesh)
organizations.description: Government ministry of Bangladesh responsible for police, border security and internal affairs; headed by Salahuddin Ahmed since February 2026.

organizations.name: Anti-Corruption Commission (Bangladesh)
organizations.description: Government-linked anti-corruption agency of Bangladesh, established in 2004; investigated scores of political figures including Sheikh Hasina after the 2024 change of government.

organizations.name: National Human Rights Commission of Bangladesh
organizations.description: Autonomous national human rights body of Bangladesh, established in 2007 and reconstituted by the National Human Rights Commission Act 2009.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Public Service Commission
organizations.description: Constitutional authority responsible for recruiting civil servants for the government of Bangladesh.

organizations.name: National Board of Revenue
organizations.description: Bangladesh's national revenue authority under the Ministry of Finance, responsible for tax and customs collection; founded 1972.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Export Processing Zones Authority
organizations.description: Government agency of Bangladesh managing the export processing zones and promoting export-oriented investment.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission
organizations.description: Independent statutory commission regulating the telecommunications sector of Bangladesh, including licensing of mobile operators.

organizations.name: Civil Aviation Authority of Bangladesh
organizations.description: Regulatory authority for civil aviation in Bangladesh, operating the country's airports.

organizations.name: Rajdhani Unnayan Kartripakkha
organizations.description: Dhaka's capital development authority, responsible for city planning, building approvals and land development in the capital; founded 1987.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Power Development Board
organizations.description: Government organization for developing and operating Bangladesh's power generation and transmission infrastructure; founded 1972.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Railway
organizations.description: State-owned railway agency of Bangladesh operating the national rail network, under the Ministry of Railways since the 2026 government allocated a separate Railway Ministry.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority
organizations.description: Authority controlling inland water transport and river routes in Bangladesh; founded 1958.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Post Office
organizations.description: State postal service provider of Bangladesh, founded 1971.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Police
organizations.description: law enforcement agency

organizations.name: Rapid Action Battalion
organizations.description: Elite anti-crime and anti-terrorism law enforcement unit of Bangladesh Police, formed 2004; sanctioned by the US in 2021 over human-rights concerns and was subject of dissolution debate after the 2024 uprising.

organizations.name: Criminal Investigation Department
organizations.description: Investigative unit of Bangladesh Police responsible for serious crime investigation; founded 1971.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Armed Forces
organizations.description: Combined military forces of Bangladesh, comprising the Army, Navy and Air Force. During the 2024 transition the military under Gen. Waker-uz-Zaman played a central role; the Armed Forces Division and Defence Ministry are headed by PM Tarique Rahman since February 2026.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Army
organizations.description: Land warfare branch of the Bangladesh Armed Forces, the largest service branch.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Navy
organizations.description: Naval warfare branch of the Bangladesh Armed Forces.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Air Force
organizations.description: Air warfare branch of the Bangladesh Armed Forces.

organizations.name: Directorate General of Forces Intelligence
organizations.description: Defence intelligence agency of the Bangladesh Armed Forces; the country's principal military intelligence body.

organizations.name: National Security Intelligence
organizations.description: National civilian intelligence agency of Bangladesh, under the National Security Council setup.

organizations.name: Border Guard Bangladesh
organizations.description: Border security paramilitary force of Bangladesh responsible for guarding the country's land borders; under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

organizations.name: Inter Services Public Relations (Bangladesh)
organizations.description: Media and public relations wing of the Bangladesh Armed Forces; founded 1972.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation
organizations.description: Bangladesh government corporation for importing, refining and distributing petroleum and oil products; parent of state oil marketing companies (Jamuna Oil, Padma Oil, Meghna Petroleum).
organizations.parent_organization: Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources

organizations.name: Petrobangla
organizations.description: National gas corporation of Bangladesh (Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation), overseeing exploration, production and distribution of natural gas.
aliases: Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation

organizations.name: Biman Bangladesh Airlines
organizations.description: National flag carrier airline of Bangladesh, wholly state-owned; founded 1972.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Chemical Industries Corporation
organizations.description: State-owned chemical industry holding corporation of Bangladesh (fertilizers, paper, chemicals) under the Ministry of Industries.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Steel and Engineering Corporation
organizations.description: Corporation owned by the Government of Bangladesh grouping state enterprises in steel, engineering and electrical manufacturing under the Ministry of Industries.

organizations.name: Titas Gas
organizations.description: Largest natural gas distribution company in Bangladesh, a Petrobangla subsidiary.

organizations.name: Jamuna Oil Company
organizations.description: State-owned petroleum marketing company of Bangladesh, a subsidiary of Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Telecommunications Company Limited
organizations.description: Government-owned largest fixed-line telecom operator in Bangladesh; incorporated as a public limited company in 2008.

organizations.name: Teletalk
organizations.description: State-run mobile phone operator of Bangladesh, the only government-owned mobile carrier.

organizations.name: BAPEX
organizations.description: Government-owned company for petroleum exploration and production in Bangladesh, a Petrobangla subsidiary.
aliases: Bangladesh Petroleum Exploration and Production Company Limited

organizations.name: Bangladesh Ordnance Factories
organizations.description: State-owned Bangladeshi defence company manufacturing small arms and ammunition, managed with army oversight; founded 1970.

organizations.name: Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited
organizations.description: State company operating the Dhaka Metro Rail (MRT Line 6) mass transit system, under the Road Transport and Highways Division.

organizations.name: BEXIMCO
organizations.description: Bangladeshi multinational conglomerate, the largest listed group on the Dhaka Stock Exchange, spanning textiles, pharmaceuticals, ceramics and energy; founded 1972 by the brothers Salman F Rahman and Sohail F Rahman.

organizations.name: Square Pharmaceuticals
organizations.description: Largest pharmaceutical company of Bangladesh, flagship of the Square Group; listed on the DSE.

organizations.name: Bashundhara Group
organizations.description: Bangladeshi industrial conglomerate with interests in real estate, cement, paper, steel, media and consumer products; founded 1987 by Ahmed Akbar Sobhan.

organizations.name: PRAN-RFL Group
organizations.description: Bangladeshi conglomerate specializing in multinational consumer goods and agribusiness (PRAN foods, RFL plastics/housewares); one of the country's largest exporters.

organizations.name: S. Alam Group of Industries
organizations.description: Bangladeshi industrial conglomerate (steel, cement, shipping, food) long chaired by Saiful Alam Masroor; was the controlling shareholder of Islami Bank Bangladesh and faced major asset seizures and probes after the 2024 fall of the Hasina government.

organizations.name: Walton Group
organizations.description: Bangladeshi electronics manufacturer (smartphones, refrigerators, motorcycles) under R.B Group; the country's leading domestic electronics brand.

organizations.name: Transcom Group
organizations.description: Bangladeshi conglomerate in beverages (Pepsi bottling), media (Mediastar/Prothom Alo, Maasranga) and retail; founded by S. S. Latifur Rahman.

organizations.name: Akij Group
organizations.description: Bangladeshi multinational conglomerate (FMCG, tobacco, textiles, ceramics); founded 1940 by Sheikh Akij Uddin.

organizations.name: Meghna Group of Industries
organizations.description: Bangladeshi business group in consumer goods, edible oil, cement and shipping; founded 1989.

organizations.name: Summit Group
organizations.description: Bangladeshi conglomerate focused on power generation, gas, telecommunications infrastructure and ports.

organizations.name: Kazi Farms Group
organizations.description: Bangladeshi agribusiness group (poultry, feed, food brands); founded 1996.

organizations.name: Rahimafrooz
organizations.description: Bangladeshi group manufacturing batteries and electrical products, active in energy retail; founded 1954.

organizations.name: M. M. Ispahani Limited
organizations.description: One of Bangladesh's oldest conglomerates (tea, real estate, textiles), founded 1820, based in Chattogram.

organizations.name: Grameenphone
organizations.description: Largest telecommunications company in Bangladesh (Telenor-affiliated), listed on the Dhaka Stock Exchange; about 2,100 employees.

organizations.name: Robi Axiata Limited
organizations.description: Second-largest mobile network operator of Bangladesh, majority-owned by Axiata Group (Malaysia).

organizations.name: Banglalink
organizations.description: Third mobile operator of Bangladesh, owned by VEON (Netherlands); founded 1996.

organizations.name: Incepta Pharmaceuticals
organizations.description: Major Bangladeshi pharmaceutical manufacturer, among the country's top pharma exporters.

organizations.name: Aarong
organizations.description: Bangladeshi retail chain of BRAC specializing in Bengali handicrafts and ethnic wear, supporting rural artisans; founded 1978.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Bank
organizations.description: Central bank of Bangladesh and chief regulatory authority of the banking sector, established 1971; led the banking-sector clean-up (including the five-bank shariah merger) after the 2024 change of government.

organizations.name: BRAC Bank
organizations.description: Private commercial bank in Bangladesh founded by BRAC, known for SME banking and parent of mobile financial service bKash.

organizations.name: Islami Bank Bangladesh
organizations.description: Shariah-based bank in Bangladesh and historically the country's largest private bank; was controlled by S. Alam Group interests until state intervention after August 2024.

organizations.name: Sammilito Islami Bank
organizations.description: State-owned commercial bank created by the merger of five troubled shariah-based private banks (First Security Islami, EXIM, Social Islami, Global Islami, Union Bank); licensed November 2025 and operating as a single entity from January 2026, becoming the largest Islamic bank in Bangladesh.

organizations.name: Dutch-Bangla Bank
organizations.description: Private-sector bank in Bangladesh, known for its Rocket mobile banking service.

organizations.name: Sonali Bank
organizations.description: Largest state-owned commercial banking institution of Bangladesh.

organizations.name: Janata Bank
organizations.description: State-owned commercial bank of Bangladesh.

organizations.name: Agrani Bank
organizations.description: State-owned commercial bank of Bangladesh, founded 1972.

organizations.name: Eastern Bank PLC
organizations.description: Leading private commercial bank in Bangladesh.

organizations.name: The City Bank
organizations.description: Private commercial bank in Bangladesh, among the first to issue cards and digital banking services.

organizations.name: IDLC Finance PLC
organizations.description: Largest non-bank financial institution (NBFI) of Bangladesh, providing corporate and retail finance.

organizations.name: Grameen Bank
organizations.description: Microfinance organization and community development bank founded in 1983 by Nobel laureate Muhammad Yunus; co-winner of the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize. Yunus led the interim government 2024-2026.

organizations.name: bKash
organizations.description: Mobile financial service (MFS) provider of Bangladesh, the country's dominant mobile money platform; subsidiary of BRAC Bank.

organizations.name: Dhaka Stock Exchange
organizations.description: Main stock exchange of Bangladesh, located in Motijheel, Dhaka; regulator is the Bangladesh Securities and Exchange Commission.

organizations.name: Sadharan Bima Corporation
organizations.description: State-owned non-life insurer and reinsurer of Bangladesh.

organizations.name: BRAC
organizations.description: International development organisation based in Bangladesh, founded 1972 by Fazle Hasan Abed; the world's largest non-governmental development organisation by employees, active in microfinance, education, health and enterprise.

organizations.name: Association for Social Advancement
organizations.description: Bangladeshi microfinance institution and NGO founded 1978, one of the country's largest microcredit providers.

organizations.name: Ain o Salish Kendra
organizations.description: Bangladeshi human rights and legal aid organization founded 1986.

organizations.name: Transparency International Bangladesh
organizations.description: Bangladeshi civil society organization affiliated with Transparency International, focused on anti-corruption and governance research.

organizations.name: Gonoshasthaya Kendra
organizations.description: Bangladeshi public-health NGO founded 1972 by Zafrullah Chowdhury, known for rural healthcare and pharmaceutical policy advocacy.

organizations.name: Dhaka Ahsania Mission
organizations.description: Bangladeshi non-governmental organisation working in education, health and community development, founded 1958 by Khan Bahadur Ahsanullah.

organizations.name: Odhikar
organizations.description: Bangladeshi human rights organisation; its documentation of abuses drew government reprisals, and its registration was cancelled in 2022 (contested in courts).

organizations.name: Manusher Jonno Foundation
organizations.description: Bangladeshi human rights and governance grant-making foundation.

organizations.name: Acid Survivors Foundation
organizations.description: Bangladeshi NGO founded 1999 supporting survivors of acid violence and advocating acid-crime legislation.

organizations.name: Friendship
organizations.description: Bangladeshi NGO founded 2002 (by Runa Khan) serving remote char and coastal communities with health, education and climate-adaptation programmes.

organizations.name: University of Dhaka
organizations.description: Oldest and premier public university of Bangladesh, founded 1921; historically the epicentre of national political movements, including the 2024 July uprising.

organizations.name: Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology
organizations.description: Top public engineering university of Bangladesh in Dhaka, tracing origins to 1876.

organizations.name: University of Chittagong
organizations.description: Public university in Chattogram, Bangladesh; founded 1966, one of the largest residential universities of the country.

organizations.name: University of Rajshahi
organizations.description: Public university in Rajshahi, Bangladesh; founded 1954, the country's second-largest university.

organizations.name: Jahangirnagar University
organizations.description: Public residential university in Savar near Dhaka; founded 1970.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Agricultural University
organizations.description: First public agricultural university in Bangladesh, founded 1961 in Mymensingh.

organizations.name: Shahjalal University of Science and Technology
organizations.description: Public university in Sylhet specializing in science and technology; founded 1987.

organizations.name: Bangladesh University of Professionals
organizations.description: Armed forces controlled public university of Bangladesh, founded 2008, offering programmes in security studies, business and medicine.

organizations.name: Military Institute of Science and Technology
organizations.description: Advanced engineering institution of the Bangladesh Armed Forces, founded 1998 in Dhaka.

organizations.name: North South University
organizations.description: First private university of Bangladesh (founded 1992), located in Dhaka; consistently among the top-ranked private universities.

organizations.name: BRAC University
organizations.description: Private university in Dhaka founded 2001 by BRAC, one of the leading research universities in the country.

organizations.name: Independent University, Bangladesh
organizations.description: Private university in Dhaka founded 1993; host institution of the International Centre for Climate Change and Development.

organizations.name: Daffodil International University
organizations.description: Private university in Dhaka founded 2002.

organizations.name: American International University-Bangladesh
organizations.description: Private university in Dhaka founded 1994, known for engineering and computer science programmes.

organizations.name: icddr,b
organizations.description: International health research organisation located in Dhaka, world-renowned for diarrhoeal disease treatment (ORS innovation) and public health research.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
organizations.description: State research organization of Bangladesh coordinating scientific and industrial research laboratories; founded 1973.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Institute of Development Studies
organizations.description: Government research institute in Bangladesh for development economics and policy research; founded 1957.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Institute of International and Strategic Studies
organizations.description: Research institute in Bangladesh on international affairs and strategic studies, founded 1978 under the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

organizations.name: Centre for Policy Dialogue
organizations.description: Dhaka-based civil society think tank on economic policy and public accountability, founded 1993 by Rehman Sobhan.

organizations.name: International Centre for Climate Change and Development
organizations.description: Research centre based at Independent University, Bangladesh, founded 2009, focused on climate change adaptation and loss and damage, led by Saleemul Huq until his death in 2023.

organizations.name: Prothom Alo
organizations.description: Largest Bengali-language daily newspaper in the world (published by Mediastar Ltd of Transcom Group), founded 1998; most widely circulated daily in Bangladesh.

organizations.name: The Daily Star (Bangladesh)
organizations.description: Leading English-language daily newspaper in Bangladesh, founded 1991.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Sangbad Sangstha
organizations.description: Bangladesh's national state-owned news agency, founded 1972.

organizations.name: United News of Bangladesh
organizations.description: Bangladesh's first and largest private-sector news agency, founded 1988.

organizations.name: bdnews24.com
organizations.description: Bangladeshi online news portal founded 2005, publishing in Bengali and English.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Television
organizations.description: State-owned television network of Bangladesh, the national broadcaster.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Betar
organizations.description: Public radio broadcaster of Bangladesh, the state-owned national radio service.

organizations.name: Daily Ittefaq
organizations.description: One of the oldest Bengali daily newspapers of Bangladesh (founded 1953 during the Language Movement era, current entity since 1972), published by Ittefaq Group.

organizations.name: Daily Jugantor
organizations.description: Major Bengali daily newspaper of Bangladesh.

organizations.name: Kaler Kantho
organizations.description: National Bengali daily newspaper founded 2010, published by East West Media Group (Bashundhara Group).

organizations.name: Bangladesh Pratidin
organizations.description: Bengali-language independent daily newspaper founded 2010, among the highest-circulation dailies of Bangladesh.

organizations.name: NTV (Bangladesh)

organizations.name: Bangladesh Nationalist Party
organizations.description: Centre-right political party founded 1978 by Ziaur Rahman; won a landslide (209 seats, two-thirds majority) in the February 2026 general election and leads the Tarique Rahman government. Ideology: Bangladeshi nationalism.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Awami League
organizations.description: Founded 1949, the party of Bangladesh's independence leadership; ruled 2009-2024 under Sheikh Hasina whose government fell in the August 2024 uprising. The party was subsequently banned from political activity and was barred from the February 2026 election; Hasina lives in exile in India.

organizations.name: Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami
organizations.description: Islamist political party (ideology: Islamism), led by Ameer Shafiqur Rahman; finished second in the February 2026 election at the head of an 11-party alliance with the National Citizen Party, becoming principal opposition and Leader of the Opposition for the first time.
aliases: 孟加拉国伊斯兰大会党

organizations.name: National Citizen Party
organizations.description: Political party founded in February 2025 by leaders of the 2024 July uprising student movement; contested the February 2026 election in alliance with Jamaat-e-Islami (11-party alliance) and won seats in the 13th Jatiya Sangsad.

organizations.name: Jatiya Party (Ershad)
organizations.description: Political party founded 1986 by Hussain Muhammad Ershad, formerly a perennial kingmaker in Bangladeshi coalitions.

organizations.name: Communist Party of Bangladesh
organizations.description: Political party of Bangladesh espousing communism, founded 1968 as a breakaway from the East Pakistan Communist Party.

organizations.name: Jatiya Samajtantrik Dal
organizations.description: Socialist political party in Bangladesh founded 1972; several factions exist (JSD, Jatiyo Samajtantrik Dal-JSD).

organizations.name: Workers Party of Bangladesh
organizations.description: Bangladeshi political party espousing socialism, founded 1980.

organizations.name: Islami Andolan Bangladesh
organizations.description: Islamist political party in Bangladesh led by Mufti Fazlul Karim's movement, a significant religious-political force in elections.

organizations.name: Gano Forum
organizations.description: Bangladeshi political party founded 1992 by Kamal Hossain, historically associated with the pro-democracy movement.

organizations.name: Bikalpa Dhara Bangladesh
organizations.description: Bangladeshi political party founded 2004 by former president A. Q. M. Badruddoza Chowdhury.

organizations.name: Liberal Democratic Party (Bangladesh)
organizations.description: Bangladeshi political party founded 2006 by Oli Ahmed; its leader Oli Ahmad was the opposition candidate in the August 2026 presidential election, receiving 88 votes.

organizations.name: Parbatya Chattagram Jana Sanghati Samiti
organizations.description: Regional political party of the Chittagong Hill Tracts indigenous peoples, founded 1972-73 by Manabendra Narayan Larma; signed the 1997 CHT Peace Accord.
aliases: United People's Party of the Chittagong Hill Tracts

organizations.name: BIMSTEC

aliases: Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation

organizations.name: Centre on Integrated Rural Development for Asia and the Pacific
organizations.description: Bangladesh-based intergovernmental organization for integrated rural development, headquartered at Chameli House, Topkhana Road, Dhaka; serves member countries across Asia-Pacific.

organizations.name: International Jute Study Group
organizations.description: Intergovernmental commodity body for jute, headquartered in Dhaka under the UN framework, promoting the global jute economy.

organizations.name: SAARC Agricultural Centre
organizations.description: SAARC (South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation) apex regional centre for agriculture, located on the BARC campus in Farmgate, Dhaka; one of the SAARC regional centres hosted by Bangladesh (SAARC's main secretariat is in Kathmandu, Nepal). Bangladesh is a SAARC founding member. Bangladesh is NOT a member of APEC.

organizations.name: South Asian Football Federation
organizations.description: Association football governing body for South Asia, headquartered in Dhaka; founded 1997, organizes the SAFF Championship.
